title: [v0.4.x] Cleanup: remove orphaned owned runtime resources
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Current triage — outstanding pre-freeze work

Milestone: **v0.4.x**; final semantic acceptance: #174. Original v0.4.20/v0.4.21/v0.4.24 references below describe the historical report, not proof of completion or a new release assignment.

Keep open for the remaining native orphan inventory/classification and cleanup evidence, including the concrete residue reported in the existing comment. Related current lifecycle work belongs to #872 / #881. Removal requires verified installation/target/resource ownership; a BaseHarbor-looking name or an unknown discovered target alone must never grant destruction authority. Verify retained workload data versus unwanted networks, foreign-resource preservation and deduplicated preservation output on Docker and Podman. Scoped or historical cleanup receipts do not automatically close all these acceptance criteria.

---

## Bug

`baha destroy --all --yes` can report `Registered deployments: 0` while BaseHarbor-owned runtime projects still exist.

The current full-destroy flow removes resources reachable from deployment/provider/state metadata, then only audits residual containers. If deployment state was already lost, incomplete or removed, orphaned projects such as `bh-local-<app>-<env>`, `bh-local-dev-gateway-dev` or stale shared modules are detected but never destroyed.

Example residuals include runtime broker/workload, dev gateway, OpenBao/PostgreSQL/Prometheus/SeaweedFS and shared Valkey modules.

## Root cause

`destroyTargetBestEffort` performs provider/state-specific cleanup and then:

1. `ListRuntimeContainers`
2. `targetOwnedRuntimeContainers`
3. fail `runtime-audit` when residual BaseHarbor containers exist

There is no fallback cleanup step between detection and audit.

## Required behavior

For full installation destroy only:

- after normal semantic/state cleanup, discover residual projects from runtime containers;
- restrict candidates to the target-owned BaseHarbor namespace (`bh-<target>-*`);
- for each residual project use the provider-neutral ownership API:
  - `ListOwnedProjectResources(project)`
  - `DestroyOwnedProjectResources(project, resources)`
  - verify `ListOwnedProjectResources(project)` is empty;
- then perform the final runtime audit;
- preserve state only if owned resources still cannot be removed/verified.

This fallback must not target non-BaseHarbor projects and must not rely on missing Compose/Quadlet files.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `destroy --all --yes` removes orphaned app/runtime-broker projects even with zero registered deployments.
- [ ] orphaned shared/provider/dev-gateway projects are removed when ownership labels identify them as BaseHarbor-owned.
- [ ] foreign projects are untouched.
- [ ] provider-neutral for Docker and Podman through RuntimeProvider ownership APIs.
- [ ] residual resources are verified after deletion.
- [ ] XDG state is removed only after the runtime audit is clean.
- [ ] focused tests + go vet pass.
- [ ] lands directly in active v0.4.21.

comments.body: Additional v0.4.23 Docker-rootless evidence: `baha up --yes --plain` → `baha app destroy --yes` → outside repository `baha destroy --all --yes` leaves `bh-local-baseharbor-demo-dev_demo-app-state` (preserved app data) and network `bh-local-baseharbor-demo-observability` with no named residue in destroy output. Recovery file `PRESERVED` reported twice. Required v0.4.24: inventory managed orphan resource names after registry deletion, distinguish intentionally preserved workload data from unwanted orphan networks, don't remove foreign resources, report all residuals explicitly and deduplicate preservation messages. Regression: full destroy after app destroy, Docker/Podman.
